site_contract.pricing_rule: Do not invent a pricing coefficient before the site pricing engine exposes a matching key.

policy.rule: A source being accessible does not make a claim publishable; admission, entailment and placement remain separate gates.

composition_principles.open_closed: Reuse or adapt an owner module before creating a new module. New modules are allowed only when the domain object is not represented by an existing asset.
composition_principles.decentralization_gate: If a conventional database, cloud or signed-record architecture satisfies the named verifier and trust boundary, prefer the simpler architecture.

shared_module_catalog.function: Map parties that cannot simply trust one another and name the property a third party must verify.
PROPERTY → VERIFIER → SOURCE → TRUST BOUNDARY → MINIMUM MECHANISM.
Bind a bounded property to a signature, hash, attestation or ledger commitment when justified.
Change control for rules, schemas, validators, keys and recovery.
Source authority, identity, frequency, owner and scope.
Grain, keys, invariants, schemas and bounded contexts.
Versioned transformations, checkpoints and failure states.
Executable invariants and pre-written acceptance gates.
Traversable provenance from input through transformation to result or decision.
Queryable evidence records and auditable APIs.
Separate technical mechanism, sensitive-data boundary, human authority and regulatory authority.
Explicit human validation boundary for consequential workflows.
Threats, trust assumptions, permissions and attack paths.
Make assurance conditions part of promotion/release rather than a late report.
Versioned cases, thresholds and comparison across changes.
Execution provenance adapted into a compute execution receipt.

decentralized-science.title: Decentralized Science & Verifiable Research Infrastructure
decentralized-science.promise: Rendre une affirmation scientifique reconstructible, reproductible et vérifiable par un tiers nommé sans déplacer inutilement les données sensibles.
decentralized-science.primary_object: scientific claim and its evidence chain
decentralized-science.mechanism: QUESTION → CLAIM → EVIDENCE → PROVENANCE → COMPUTATION → ATTESTATION → VERIFICATION

new_modules.function: Study → protocol → dataset → transformation → result → claim → evidence.
Claim-evidence graph connecting result, dataset, code, environment, contributor and attestation.
Controlled access boundary separating sensitive data from shared provenance/verification metadata.
Receipt stating who verified which property of which research artifact under which version.
Change control for schemas, validation rules, reviewers and disputes.
Independent-verification acceptance gate for a named scientific property.

offers.name: Research Trust & Feasibility Diagnostic
offers.trigger: A consequential research claim or workflow matters, but the trust boundary and verifier are unclear.
offers.outcome: Decide whether independent verification or a decentralized mechanism is justified.

offers.name: Verifiable Research Protocol Architecture Sprint
offers.trigger: Several organizations need to inspect provenance, computation, attribution or evidence without collapsing data ownership.
offers.outcome: Specify the minimum viable verifiable-research architecture and its acceptance tests.
acceptance: data plane vs evidence plane separated

offers.name: Reproducible Evidence Pipeline PoC
offers.trigger: The architecture needs one bounded end-to-end proof before platform investment.
offers.outcome: Demonstrate one claim path from source to independently inspectable evidence and replay.
acceptance: one bounded run reproducible under documented environment

offers.name: Decentralized Science Infrastructure Implementation
offers.trigger: A bounded PoC has a justified production path and named operating owners.
offers.outcome: Implement reusable provenance, access, verification and governance infrastructure around research workflows.

offers.name: DeSci Protocol Assurance & Evidence Review
offers.trigger: An existing protocol makes verification, provenance or reproducibility claims that need technical scrutiny.
offers.outcome: Classify protocol claims as supported, bounded or unsupported and make findings retestable.
acceptance: every finding linked to an inspectable artifact

decentralized-compute.title: Decentralized Compute Engineering
decentralized-compute.promise: Distribuer un workload seulement quand la contrainte de confiance, souveraineté, résilience ou vérification justifie la complexité, puis rendre l’exécution mesurable et inspectable.
decentralized-compute.mechanism: WORKLOAD → PROPERTY → TRUST BOUNDARY → MINIMUM VERIFICATION MECHANISM → EXECUTION → RECEIPT → VERIFIER

new_modules.function: Providers, nodes, regions, accelerators, trust and failure domains.
Workload identity, code/model hash, node, environment, inputs, outputs and attestation.
Select signatures, remote attestation, TEE, ZK or replication from the property to verify.
Decision asset selecting the minimum privacy/correctness mechanism instead of assuming a universal winner.
Matched workload benchmark across candidate architectures with an explicit metric contract.
Failure, retry, replication, provider exit and centralized fallback plan.
Optional scheduling/provider/pricing adapter when a resource market is actually required.
Node/environment identity and attestation for the execution receipt.
Throughput, latency, availability, cost and verification-overhead envelope for a bounded workload.

offers.name: Workload Decentralization Diagnostic
offers.trigger: A workload is proposed for distributed/decentralized execution, but the reason centralization is insufficient is not yet proven.
offers.outcome: Decide whether to centralize, distribute, prototype a verification mechanism, or stop the decentralized path.

offers.name: Distributed & Verifiable Compute Architecture Sprint
offers.trigger: Execution must span providers or be independently verifiable under a named trust boundary.
offers.outcome: Specify topology, verifier, failure model and minimum verification mechanism.

offers.name: Verifiable Execution PoC
offers.trigger: The architecture needs measured evidence on one representative workload.
offers.outcome: Run a matched workload and produce an independently inspectable execution receipt and benchmark.

offers.name: Decentralized Compute Infrastructure Implementation
offers.trigger: PoC measurements justify production integration and an operating owner exists.
offers.outcome: Implement distributed execution, verification, monitoring, provider/fallback integration and release evidence.
acceptance: release gate passes on representative workloads

offers.name: Compute Protocol Assurance
offers.trigger: An existing decentralized-compute design makes trust, execution or performance claims that need independent scrutiny.
offers.outcome: Check whether architecture, benchmark and attestation evidence support the published claims.
acceptance: every numeric claim maps to a metric contract

cross_sell_routes.condition: Research computation itself must be independently verified across execution providers.
The problem is only lineage/provenance inside one trusted organization.
The dominant issue is regulated product validation rather than multi-party scientific verification.
Only shared state/programmability is required; compute stays conventional.
The workload is conventional and the dominant issue is deployment/security gating.
One trusted cloud satisfies the property and failure model.
